issues.advice: The source means 'the Dao that can be spoken is not the constant Dao; the name that can be named is not the constant name.' The translation renders it as 'the Dao is quiet/silent,' which mistranslates 可道 (can be spoken) and 非常 (not constant). Render the conditional 'can be spoken/named' and 'not the constant' meaning.

issues.span: 常無を欲して妙を観ず。常有を欲して徼を観ず
issues.advice: The source is 'constantly without desire, thereby observe its subtlety; constantly with desire, thereby observe its manifestations.' The translation reverses the structure, making 常無/常有 the object of 欲 rather than the adverb 'constantly' modifying desire/no-desire. Render as '常に欲無くして…妙を観、常に欲有して…徼を観る.'

issues.span: 此二者は同一の源から異名なり
issues.advice: Source says 同出而異名 (emerge together but differ in name). 'Same source' is acceptable but should preserve 'emerge together' (同出) and 'differ in name' (異名) more faithfully; current phrasing is loose.

issues.span: 玄を繰り返す
issues.advice: 玄之又玄 means 'mystery upon mystery' / 'darkness within darkness,' not 'repeat the mystery.' Render as '玄の又玄' or '玄にして又玄'.

issues.span: 道は言ふべからず、名は言ふべからず
issues.advice: The source says 道可道非常道 / 名可名非常名 — 'the Dao that can be spoken is not the constant Dao; the name that can be named is not the constant name.' issues.span: 常無を欲して妙を観ず、常有を欲して徼を観ず
issues.advice: The source is 常無欲以觀其妙 / 常有欲以觀其徼 — 'always without desire, in order to observe its subtlety; always with desire, in order to observe its manifestations.' The translation misparses 常無欲 as 常無 + 欲 and renders it as 'desiring the constant non-being,' inverting the sense. Parse 常無欲 / 常有欲 as 'constantly without desire / constantly with desire.'

issues.span: 此二者は同一の源より異名なり
issues.advice: Source 此兩者同出而異名 means 'these two emerge together but are named differently.' '同一の源より' ('from the same source') is acceptable in spirit but the '同出' (emerge together) nuance and the omitted 玄 (mystery) predicate are weakened; also 同謂之玄 ('both are called mystery') is dropped entirely.

issues.span: 玄にして又玄。衆妙の門。
issues.advice: Source 玄之又玄衆妙之門 means 'mystery upon mystery — the gate of all subtleties.' The translation drops the copula/relationship (e.g., これ衆妙の門なり) and the connective structure, leaving fragments that do not convey 'the gate of all wonders.' Restore the predicative link.

issues.span: 無名は天地の始なり、有名は萬物之母なり
issues.advice: Source 無名天地之始 / 有名萬物之母 — 'the nameless is the beginning of heaven and earth; the named is the mother of ten thousand things.' The translation omits 天地 (heaven and earth) as the object of 始 and 萬物 as the object of 母, reducing them to bare 'beginning' and 'mother.' Include 天地の始 / 萬物の母.

issues.span: 道は言ふべからず、名は言ふべからず

It dwells where others fear, in the place of the many; it is at the heart of the good, in the depths of the wise, and in the place of benevolence. issues.span: It dwells where others fear, in the place of the many
issues.advice: 處衆人之所惡 means 'dwells in places that people disdain/loathe,' not 'where others fear' nor 'the place of the many.' Conflates 衆人之所惡 into two clauses and mistranslates 惡 as fear.

issues.span: it is at the heart of the good, in the depths of the wise, and in the place of benevolence
issues.advice: 居善地、心善淵、與善仁 are parallel prescriptions about the sage's conduct (dwelling in good ground, heart deep as an abyss, associating with benevolence), not descriptions of water being 'at the heart of the good.' The parallel structure is broken and meaning distorted.

issues.span: For it is because it does not strive that it is the way
issues.advice: 故幾於道 means 'therefore it is close to the Way' (幾 = nearly/approaches), not 'it is the way.' Also 夫惟不爭 introduces the concluding clause; the causal rendering is acceptable but the predicate is wrong.

issues.span: governs affairs wisely
issues.advice: 政善治 refers to governing with good order/administration; 事善能 refers to handling affairs with competence. The translation collapses 政善治 and 事善能 and omits 事善能.

issues.span: the way
issues.advice: 道 as the Daoist technical term should be capitalized 'the Way' to match convention and distinguish from ordinary 'way.'

issues.span: in the place of the many; it is at the heart of the good, in the depths of the wise, and in the place of benevolence
issues.advice: Repetitive 'in the place of' and mixed metaphors reduce readability; the parallel list should be rendered as a coherent series of virtues/conducts.

issues.span: Elle habite là où les autres trouvent le malheur

issues.span: la voie

issues.span: un fond profond, une bonté, une parole de foi

issues.span: C'est pourquoi, en ne se battant pas, elle est la Voie.
issues.advice: The source says 夫惟不爭 (only because it does not contend) — it does not say 'elle est la Voie'. The clause is truncated in the source; render the non-contention idea without asserting identity with the Way.

issues.span: un gouvernement sage et une action capable d'agir au bon moment

issues.span: un don de bonté

issues.advice: The verb 'habite' cannot govern all these objects; the parallel 居/心/與/言/政/事/動 series needs a consistent structure (e.g. 'en son lieu, elle est bonne au choix; en son cœur, bonne à la profondeur...').

issues.span: elle ressemble à la Voie

issues.span: là où les autres trouvent le malheur

payload.translation: 上善如水：水潤物而不爭，處眾人之所惡，故幾於道。居善地，心善淵，與善仁，言善信，政善治，事善能動，時善也。夫惟不爭。

issues.span: 事善能動，時善也
issues.advice: The source lists parallel phrases: 事善能 and 動善時. The translation merges 動 into the previous phrase and renders 時善也, losing the 動善時 unit. Restore the parallel structure: 事善能，動善時.

issues.span: 水潤物而不爭
issues.advice: Source says 水善利萬物而不爭; 潤物 omits 利萬物 (benefiting all things). Render 利萬物 explicitly.

issues.span: 上善如水：

payload.translation: 上善如水：水善利萬物而不爭，處衆人之所惡，故幾於道。居善地，心善淵，與善仁，言善信，政善治，事善能，動善時。夫惟不爭。

issues.span: 夫惟不爭。
issues.advice: The source ends with '夫惟不爭' which is an incomplete clause in the Laozi (typically '夫惟不爭，故天下莫能與之爭'). issues.span: 上善如水：
issues.advice: The colon after '上善如水' is a modern editorial addition not present in the classical text; classical Chinese punctuation would typically use a comma or no punctuation. Minor, but consider using a comma for consistency with the rest of the punctuation style.

issues.span: Carrying wealth without restraint is no better than having it
issues.advice: The source 持而盈之不如其已 means 'to hold and overfill it is not as good as stopping/desisting' — the object is not 'wealth' but the act of overfilling/accumulating. Rendering 已 as 'having it' is inaccurate; it should convey 'stopping/ceasing'.

issues.span: sharpening ambition without restraint
issues.advice: 揣而銳之 refers to sharpening/hammering something to a point (a blade or point), not 'ambition'; the metaphor is about over-sharpening that cannot be sustained. Avoid introducing 'ambition'.

issues.span: one becomes proud and wastes away one's own fate
issues.advice: 自遺其咎 is 'brings blame/disaster upon oneself,' not 'wastes away one's fate.' Correct the meaning of 咎 and 自遺.

issues.span: this is the way of heaven

issues.span: Holding wealth to the full and not letting it rest
issues.advice: The source 持而盈之不如其已 means 'to hold and fill it is not as good as stopping'; the translation omits 不如其已 ('better to stop') and misreads 盈 as 'wealth' rather than 'fullness'.

issues.span: holding sharpness and not letting it grow
issues.advice: 揣而銳之不可長保 means 'hammering it sharp, it cannot be preserved long'; the translation drops 不可長保 ('cannot be long preserved') and renders it as 'not letting it grow'.

issues.span: guarding treasures and gold in a full hall
issues.advice: 金玉滿堂莫之能守 means 'gold and jade fill the hall, none can guard them'; the translation adds 'guarding' as if it were the subject's action and omits 莫之能守 ('no one can keep them').

issues.span: forgetting one's own fault
issues.advice: 自遺其咎 means 'brings disaster upon oneself' (遺 = bequeath/leave to oneself), not 'forgetting one's fault'.

issues.span: retreating from the world
issues.advice: 身退 means 'withdraw oneself / retire from one's position', not 'retreat from the world'; 天之道 is 'the way of heaven' as a concluding clause, which is fine, but the preceding clause should be 'when the work is done and fame achieved, to withdraw oneself — that is the way of heaven.'

issues.span: achieving success in merit and fame
issues.advice: Awkward nominalization; 功成名遂 is a parallel phrase meaning 'when merit is established and fame achieved'.

issues.span: the way of heaven
issues.advice: The whole rendering is a string of fragments without the causal/logical connectors (不如, 莫之能, 自遺, 天之道) that structure the passage; it reads as a list rather than a coherent aphorism.

payload.translation: Holding wealth to the full is not as good as stopping it; hammering sharpness and not letting it grow is not as good as preserving it; guarding gold and jade in a full hall is not as good as keeping them; guarding wealth and glory and being proud is not as good as avoiding blame; achieving merit and fame is not as good as retreating; when work is done and fame achieved, to withdraw oneself — that is the way of heaven.

issues.span: hammering sharpness and not letting it grow is not as good as preserving it
issues.advice: The source 揣而銳之不可長保 means 'hammering something sharp cannot be preserved for long' — the 'not as good as preserving it' clause is invented and reverses the sense; render as 'a sharpened edge cannot be kept long'.

issues.span: guarding gold and jade in a full hall is not as good as keeping them
issues.advice: Source 金玉滿堂莫之能守 means 'gold and jade filling the hall — no one can guard them'; the 'not as good as keeping them' is a mistranslation that contradicts the original.

issues.span: guarding wealth and glory and being proud is not as good as avoiding blame

issues.span: achieving merit and fame is not as good as retreating
issues.advice: Source 功成名遂身退天之道 means 'when merit is achieved and fame accomplished, to withdraw the self — that is the way of heaven'; the 'not as good as retreating' is a spurious comparison not in the source.

issues.span: Holding wealth to the full is not as good as stopping it

issues.span: not as good as ... not as good as ... not as good as ... not as good as

payload.translation: The ancient sages of the way were subtle, mysterious, and profound, yet beyond the grasp of the wise. For it is because they are beyond the grasp of the wise that they have assumed the form of the gentle and the easy. Like a traveler crossing a river in winter, they were cautious and wary of their neighbors. Like a guest, they were open and transparent, like ice about to melt, like the raw wood of a tree, like the valley of a stream, like the turbid water of a river. Who can make the turbid become still? Who can make the still become clear? Who can make the moving become still? Who can make the still become long-lasting? The one who holds this way does not desire to be full. For it is because they do not desire to be full that they can endure without change.

issues.span: beyond the grasp of the wise
issues.advice: 深不可識 means 'so deep as to be unknowable/inscrutable', not 'beyond the grasp of the wise'; remove the added 'wise' and render as 'too deep to be known'.

issues.span: 豫若冬涉川猶若畏四鄰
issues.advice: These are two distinct similes: 'hesitant like one crossing a river in winter' and 'cautious like one fearing the four neighbors'. The translation merges them and drops the 'four neighbors' image; render both separately.

issues.span: 儼若客渙若冰將釋敦兮其若樸曠兮其若谷渾兮其若濁
issues.advice: The sequence of similes is misassigned: 儼若客 = 'dignified/serious like a guest', 渙若冰將釋 = 'yielding like ice about to melt', 敦兮其若樸 = 'simple like uncarved wood', 曠兮其若谷 = 'open like a valley', 渾兮其若濁 = 'murky like turbid water'. The translation attaches 'open and transparent' to the guest and scrambles the rest.

issues.span: 孰能濁以靜之徐清孰能安以乆動之徐生
issues.advice: The two rhetorical questions are 'Who can, from turbidity, still it and slowly clarify it?' and 'Who can, from stability, long move it and slowly give life?' The translation splits each into two separate questions and loses the causal 'thereby' structure.

issues.span: 故能弊不新成
issues.advice: This means 'thus they can be worn out/old without needing new completion' (i.e., they do not seek renewal), not 'endure without change'; render the sense of 弊 (worn, old) and 不新成 (not newly completed).

issues.span: the way
issues.advice: 道 here is the Dao; capitalize as 'the Way' to match standard rendering of the Daodejing term.

issues.span: 善為士者
issues.advice: '士' is 'the one who is good at being a master/scholar' — render as 'the ancient masters who were skilled in the Way' rather than 'sages of the way'.

issues.span: they have assumed the form of the gentle and the easy
issues.advice: 彊為之容 means 'I am forced to describe their appearance'; the translation invents 'form of the gentle and the easy' and shifts to present perfect, breaking the flow.

payload.translation: The ancients who were skilled in the Way were subtle, mysterious, profound, yet too deep to be known. For it is precisely because they are too deep to be known that they have assumed the form of the gentle and the easy. Like a traveler crossing a river in winter, they were cautious and wary of their neighbors. Like a guest, they were open and transparent, like ice about to melt, like uncarved wood, like a valley, like turbid water. Who can make the turbid still? Who can make the still clear? Who can make the moving still? Who can make the still long-lasting? The one who holds this Way does not desire to be full. For it is because they do not desire to be full that they can endure without change.

issues.span: they have assumed the form of the gentle and the easy
issues.advice: The source 故彊為之容 means 'therefore one is forced to describe their appearance'; 彊 (qiǎng) means 'forced/compelled', not 'gentle'. The translation misreads 彊 as 'gentle' and drops the sense of reluctant description.

issues.span: Like a traveler crossing a river in winter, they were cautious and wary of their neighbors.
issues.advice: 豫若冬涉川猶若畏四鄰 contains two separate similes: 'hesitant like one crossing a river in winter' and 'cautious like one fearing the four neighbors'. The translation merges them and omits the distinct 豫 (hesitant) image.

issues.span: Like a guest, they were open and transparent, like ice about to melt
issues.advice: 儼若客 means 'dignified/reserved like a guest', not 'open and transparent'. 渙若冰將釋 means 'scattered/dissolving like ice about to melt'. The translation misassigns the guest simile and drops 儼 (dignified).

issues.span: Who can make the turbid still? Who can make the still clear? Who can make the moving still? Who can make the still long-lasting?
issues.advice: The source 孰能濁以靜之徐清孰能安以乆動之徐生 means 'Who can, from turbidity, by stillness, gradually become clear? Who can, from stability, through long movement, gradually give birth?' The translation reverses the causal relations and invents 'make the moving still' and 'make the still long-lasting', which are not in the text.

issues.span: they can endure without change
issues.advice: 故能弊不新成 means 'therefore they can be worn out/old without needing to be newly completed' — i.e., they can remain un-renewed. 'Endure without change' is a loose paraphrase that loses 弊 (worn) and 新成 (newly completed).

issues.span: skilled in the Way
issues.advice: 善為士者 refers to 'those skilled as scholars/officers' (士), not 'skilled in the Way'. 為士 is about being a person of worth, not mastery of the Way.

issues.span: For it is precisely because they are too deep to be known that they have assumed the form of the gentle and the easy.
issues.advice: The sentence is convoluted and the causal chain is unclear; restructure for readability while preserving the 'forced to describe' sense.

issues.span: the gentle and the easy
issues.advice: This renders 容 (appearance/demeanor) as a moral quality, losing the classical sense of describing outward form; also the Daoist paradox of 不欲盈 (not desiring fullness) is flattened.

payload.translation: I am writing a biography of Ah Q, and it has been more than a couple of years. Yet, while I am writing, I am also constantly recalling it, which clearly shows that I am not a man of "establishing a name." For an immortal pen must be used by an immortal person, so people transmit through writing, and writing transmits through people. Ultimately, who transmits whom, has become increasingly unclear, and finally, it all boils down to transmitting Ah Q, as if there were ghosts in my thoughts.

issues.span: I am writing a biography of Ah Q, and it has been more than a couple of years
issues.advice: The source means the narrator has been intending/planning to write the biography for over a year or two, not that the writing has been ongoing for that long. Render the temporal sense as 'It has been more than a year or two since I wanted to write a proper biography of Ah Q.'

issues.span: while I am writing, I am also constantly recalling it
issues.advice: '往回想' means to think back / reconsider / hesitate, not 'recall it' (the biography). Convey the sense of second thoughts or turning things over in one's mind.

issues.span: a man of "establishing a name"
issues.advice: '立言' is a classical Confucian term (establishing words/teachings that endure), one of the 'three immortalities' (立德、立功、立言). Translate as 'a man who establishes enduring words' or 'one who founds a lasting discourse,' not 'establishing a name.'

issues.span: an immortal pen must be used by an immortal person
issues.advice: The source says an immortal pen must transmit/hand down an immortal person (不朽之笔，须传不朽之人), i.e., the enduring brush must record an enduring figure. The current rendering reverses the relation and drops 'transmit.'

issues.span: so people transmit through writing, and writing transmits through people
issues.advice: The source is '人以文传，文以人传' — a person is handed down through his writing, and the writing is handed down through the person. 'Transmit through' loses the passive 'be handed down/immortalized by' sense; render as 'the man is made enduring by his writing, and the writing by the man.'

issues.span: it all boils down to transmitting Ah Q
issues.advice: '归结到传阿Q' means the matter resolves into (my) writing the biography of Ah Q, not 'transmitting Ah Q.' Use 'writing the biography of Ah Q.'

issues.span: Ultimately, who transmits whom, has become increasingly unclear
issues.advice: Remove the comma after 'whom' and smooth the clause: 'in the end, just who is handing down whom has gradually become rather unclear.'

issues.span: as if there were ghosts in my thoughts
issues.advice: '仿佛思想里有鬼似的' is idiomatic for feeling haunted/obsessed, as if something uncanny were at work in one's mind. 'Ghosts in my thoughts' is a literal calque; consider 'as if some ghost were haunting my mind.'

payload.translation: I have been intending to write a proper biography of Ah Q for over a year or two. Yet, while I am writing, I am constantly thinking back on it, which clearly shows that I am not a man of "establishing words." For an immortal pen must be used by an immortal person, so the man is made enduring by his writing, and the writing by the man.
